## Dieses Dokument

- Datum: 15.2.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief

pages.transcription:
Taft Hotel
Newhaven, Conn

15.2.41

Dear Hanna,
Don't be surprised if Eva writes you that she had
to change school in Groton after a few days. The head-mistress
of the private, 'progressive' school (I wrote you all about it before)
was very eager to have Eva and as good as promised me a scholar-
ship for her which, as she said, would almost certainly be granted
if she wanted to accept a child. The board of trustees (by the trustees
however, only met after an unforeseen delay of a few days)
and she told Mrs Schaeffer to send Eva to her school in the meantime.
Now unfortunately the trustees decided that their resources did not
allow for another scholarship, even though the head of the school had
recommended it and so Eva had to change. I am sorry for Eva to
whom this change probably is not too welcome, although she knew that
all depended on the decision about the scholarship. But we explained
her before, and Mrs. Sch. told me she explained her again that it had
nothing to do with her personal qualities but depended on the school's
funds, and so I hope she will soon settle down in the public school
which is also supposed to be good. I have no reports yet how she
likes it, it is too soon, but some other children of Mrs Sch's also
go there and are very happy there. And as Mrs. Sch. told me that all
her children took part in all of the private school's festivals and
other functions, it will be no complete break and she will continue
to meet the friends she may have made in those few days. - I wrote you
in my last letter that I had visited Eva and found her happy
in her new surroundings and quite her old self as she was at
home, and Mrs Sch wrote me that she continues that way and is quite
"zugänglich" and satisfied. The children I met there I liked extremely
well and she certainly does not lack nice company, and Mrs. Sch of
whom both Stefan and I have a very good impression, thinks and
speaks and treats children like ourselves. Eva may go away over
the weekend once a month (have visitors or go out for the day every
Sat. and Sunday) and we will have her here as soon as we can. -
We have nearly given up hope for finding a furnished apartment,
it is extremely difficult here, and we will probably remain at this hotel.
It is not ideal, but Stefan got a nice room to work in, I do my best
not to lose myself in all the papers in the bedroom, and so we are
quite satisfied and work quite hard. There is the library very near at hand,
a long wanted pleasure, Stefan may take books home and there is no
question of being lonely. He had lunch with the head librarian and
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier. Sehr gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
his wife - a sculptor - today, both extremely nice, Thornton Wilder
and Hindemith live in Newhaven, Shalom Asch who has a house about
an hour away, dropped in two days ago, Maass is with us to day,
and several other friends live not too far away. The trains to
Newyork are a real pleasure and I can't tell you how much I
enjoy it after all that flying which is boring and makes you
tired without any special reason. - I address this letter to Bath
as we hope that you have gone there with Manfred to have a good
rest after his exam. You should not spend the spring in London, it
is so much quieter in Bath, and how lovely is spring there! I wish we
could be with you!
Tell Lotte Smollett again how sorry I was not to be
able to see her children. But it takes nearly an hour by train
to go out there, and I had lots of things to do in that short
time, I unfortunately could not manage it. My hope is that
someone will take me out in a car one day, and I certainly keep
it in mind. - About Carmel's children I wrote you some time ago.
I saw Robin and had the impression that he felt quite at home
and was on the best terms with Berner's and Rose. John who is now
with a friend of Carmel's, Tony --? seems to be really very diffi-
cult. He apparently has made up his mind to dislike everything
and is only satisfied when he goes to the movies. I have the im-
pression that Berner's and Rose really tried their best to understand
him, to please him and by discussing things with him. But he
seems to want not to like America.
I must go out now, so only kindest regards
and best love,
Lotte
